brief: Copy through an inclusive byte limit or newline and return the skipped source offset.
decl: std::uint32_t copy_line_segment(std::span<std::byte> destination, std::span<const std::byte> source, std::int32_t inclusive_limit);
notes: Original bytes and execution establish argument widths and access order.
Spans are host byte views; original 32-bit address identities are explicit where needed.

bookkeeping.scope: Complete original body on supplied scalar state and valid byte spans. Copy cases include overlapping and unaligned views with the original read/write order.
bookkeeping.supported_domain: Byte spans covering the reads/writes reached before newline or the inclusive signed limit, including tested overlap. NUL bytes do not stop copying; the return is a numeric offset, not a host pointer.
bookkeeping.acceptance: Met: 338 synthetic original-execution cases matched bit-exact by MSVC and Zig/Clang runners. See docs/recovery/record-stack.md.
